html:
On 17 May 1995 a six-year-old Tibetan boy, Gedhun Choekyi Nyima, was taken away with his family by the Chinese authorities. Three days earlier the 14th Dalai Lama had named him the 11th Panchen Lama. He has not been seen in public since.

The Panchen Lama is the second highest lama of the Gelug school, based at Tashilhunpo Monastery in Shigatse. Each Panchen Lama traditionally helps find the next Dalai Lama, and the reverse. After the 10th Panchen Lama died in 1989, the search for his successor became a contest between the Dalai Lama in exile and Beijing.

Later in 1995 the Chinese government chose another boy, Gyaincain Norbu, by drawing lots from a golden urn, a Qing era method. Most Tibetans do not accept him. China says Gedhun Choekyi Nyima lives a normal private life. The case matters because whoever controls the Panchen Lama may shape the choice of the next Dalai Lama.
